 Vietnam's e-commerce market: Sales surge, but the competition to select the right sellers intensifies.
 The Vietnamese e-commerce market continues to record impressive growth, with sales across the four major online retail platforms exceeding VND 150 trillion in Q3 2026. However, behind these growth figures lies a noteworthy paradox: sales are continuously expanding while the number of sellers generating orders is shrinking. Along with the rise of TikTok Shop and the trend of concentrating sales on official brand stores, the market is entering a phase of increasingly fierce competition and market consolidation.
 Báo Đại biểu Nhân dân • 06/11/2026 Follow Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e Add Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e 0 Over 150 trillion VND in sales in one quarter.
 According to a report from the data aggregation and mining platform Metric, total sales across the four platforms Shopee, TikTok Shop, Lazada, and Tiki reached approximately VND 150.4 trillion in the third quarter of 2026, a 45.16% increase compared to the same period last year. 
 metric This is remarkable growth in the context of a retail market witnessing significant changes in consumer behavior, customer approaches, and business strategies.
 In the first nine months of 2026, total sales across the four e-commerce platforms reached approximately VND 442 trillion, a 44.47% increase compared to the same period in 2025. These figures further affirm the increasingly important role of e-commerce in Vietnam's goods distribution system.
 However, growth in transaction volume does not necessarily mean that all market participants will benefit.
 According to Metric, in the third quarter of 2026, the number of stores generating orders on e-commerce platforms was only about 470,300, a decrease of 2.47% compared to the same period last year.
 The contrasting trends between sales volume and the number of vendors indicate a structural shift in the market. While the total value of goods traded continues to increase, sales activity tends to be more concentrated among those that maintain their competitiveness.
 This also poses challenges for small retailers. As the market becomes increasingly professional, the advantage no longer lies simply in the ability to list products, but depends more on product quality, operational capabilities, pricing strategy, marketing activities, and the ability to retain customers.
 Notably, the trend towards higher-value products is also becoming more pronounced. The sales share of products priced above 1 million VND increased from 14.5% to 19%.
 This shift shows that e-commerce is no longer just a popular shopping channel for cheap goods, but is increasingly attracting higher-value transactions. This presents opportunities for genuine brands, while also placing higher demands on reputation, product quality, and after-sales service.
 Shopee and TikTok Shop enter a fierce competition for market share.
 One of the most notable developments in the e-commerce market in Q3 2026 was the rapid narrowing of the market share gap between Shopee and TikTok Shop.
 According to Metric, if the market share difference between the two platforms was nearly 15 percentage points in the same period of 2025, by the third quarter of 2026, this gap will be just over 1 percentage point.
 This change reflects the rapid growth of TikTok Shop and also shows that Shopee's leading position is facing increasing competitive pressure.
 Notably, the two platforms are developing distinct advantages in their respective product categories. TikTok Shop dominates in men's and women's fashion , while Shopee continues to lead in the mobile phones and tablets, home appliances, and home and lifestyle categories.
 You may also like In sectors such as beauty, groceries, food, sports , travel, and health, the competition between the two platforms is direct.
 The rise of TikTok Shop also reflects a shift in how consumers access products. Instead of simply searching for goods based on readily available needs, buyers increasingly have more opportunities to discover products through short videos , livestreams, and visually engaging content.
 This forces retailers to adjust their marketing strategies, not only competing on price but also investing in content, interactivity, and the shopping experience.
 Another development is the increasing role of official brand stores. According to Metric, the Shop Mall group accounts for only 3.54% of the total number of stores but contributes 36.8% of sales on Shopee and TikTok Shop.
 This disparity highlights the significant advantage of branded retailers with stable supply sources and the ability to build trust with consumers.
 Meanwhile, domestic sellers and warehouses continue to increase their market share on Shopee. Their sales reached VND 69.8 trillion, accounting for 95.6% of total sales, up from 92.4% in the same period last year.
 Conversely, sales from foreign sellers decreased by 27.1%, to approximately VND 3,200 billion, bringing their share down from 7.6% to 4.4%.
 The above figures show that domestic sellers are consolidating their position on major e-commerce platforms. However, sales advantage does not mean a reduction in competitive pressure, especially as operating costs, advertising, and service quality requirements are increasingly becoming decisive factors in the survival of each store.
 Sales of household appliances increased by over 51%, and the market is forecast to continue its surge towards the end of the year.
 Besides the shift in market share between platforms, the Metric report also noted significant growth in several product categories.
 In the third quarter of 2026, the pet care industry achieved sales of approximately VND 1,921.5 billion, a 38.2% increase compared to the same period last year. However, sales volume decreased by 6.9%, to 22.9 million products, while the number of stores decreased by 9%, to approximately 20,700.
 The two product groups that contributed the most to sales were pet food, reaching 795 billion VND, and accessories, reaching 481.1 billion VND.
 In the home appliance sector, sales reached VND 7,966.7 billion, a 51.4% increase compared to the same period last year. Notably, production volume only increased by 2.6%, reaching 22.8 million products, while the number of showrooms decreased by 13.9%, to approximately 47,500.
 The difference between sales growth rate and production volume indicates that the value of goods consumed is trending upwards. Specifically, products priced at 1 million VND or more contributed 57.7% of the total sales of the household electrical appliance industry.
 In the brand rankings, Apple leads with sales of approximately 1.923 trillion VND, despite being the only brand in the top 10 to record negative growth. Meanwhile, Samsung grew by 98.7% and Vinamilk increased by a remarkable 225.86%.
 These developments show that competition in the online retail market is not only taking place between e-commerce platforms but is also becoming increasingly fierce between brands within each product category.
 You may also like For Q4 2026, Metric forecasts total sales across the four major e-commerce platforms could reach VND 165.5 trillion, a 10.05% increase compared to Q3. Expected sales volume is approximately 1.102 billion products, a 1.22% increase.
 The main drivers of growth came from year-end shopping events such as 11.11, 12.12, Christmas, and the demand for New Year's preparations.
 If this forecast comes true, total sales for the whole year of 2026 across the four exchanges could reach approximately 607,500 billion VND.
 However, strong growth prospects also mean greater competitive pressure. As the market increasingly focuses on sellers with strong operational capabilities and brands, increasing sales is no longer the sole measure of business performance.
 For businesses, the more important challenge is the ability to maintain profitability after deducting operating expenses, marketing costs, logistics costs, and other expenses related to selling on the platform.
 From a market perspective, the increase in transaction volume coupled with the filtering process of sellers indicates that Vietnamese e-commerce is entering a new phase of development. In this phase, the competitive advantage increasingly belongs to businesses capable of building brands, controlling product quality, and organizing business operations efficiently.
 Sales reaching hundreds of trillions of dong continue to open up significant growth potential for Vietnam's e-commerce sector, but opportunities are no longer evenly distributed. The race in the coming period will not only be a competition for market share between platforms, but also a screening of the sellers' ability to survive and thrive.
